title: Signal · Tuesday 10 November
overview: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at a lower price, Crédit Agricole proposes merging Banco BPM with its Italian arm, and Evident counts a record 111 new AI use cases at banks in the third quarter.

top.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at a lower price
top.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on 9 November, one model offered with and without strict cyber and biology safeguards. It says both generate output up to 30 percent faster than the 5.1 versions, at USD 8 per million input tokens and USD 40 per million output tokens; TechCrunch reports Fable's input price was USD 10.
top.background: Fable 5.2 runs on AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, while Mythos stays with vetted cyber and life sciences users. Box, one launch tester, said it flagged salary deposits that did not match a bank statement's balance in a loan file.
top.why: A cheaper top model on all three hyperscalers makes long, unattended document and code work easier to justify for banks that buy AI through their cloud contracts.
top.watch_next: Whether model risk teams accept Anthropic's caveat that both models more often suspect they are being tested.

top.headline: Crédit Agricole proposes merging Banco BPM with Crédit Agricole Italia
top.summary: Crédit Agricole proposed on 9 November a merger of Banco BPM and Crédit Agricole Italia, creating Italy's third-largest banking group with 6.5 million customers and more than 2,300 branches. Banco BPM shareholders would receive a 20 percent premium in the exchange ratio and a EUR 1 billion extraordinary dividend.
top.background: Crédit Agricole, which owns 29.6 percent of Banco BPM, would hold about 45 percent of the combined bank, which would stay listed in Milan under Banco BPM's chief executive. It expects EUR 800 million of yearly synergies and completion in the second half of 2027, subject to ECB and golden power approval.
top.why: A foreign shareholder leading a deal of this size tests how Rome uses its golden power rules, a question for every cross-border bank combination in Europe.
top.watch_next: Banco BPM's board response, and the shareholder vote that would spare Crédit Agricole a mandatory bid.

top.headline: Banks announced a record 111 AI use cases last quarter, Evident finds
top.summary: The 50 banks in the Evident AI Index announced 111 new AI use cases in the third quarter, a record, including 22 agentic ones. For 41 percent of them it was the bank's first AI deployment in that business line or function, yet only 21 percent disclosed an outcome, down from 27 percent in the second quarter.
top.background: Agents now draft credit memos at DBS, support anti-money laundering investigations at TD Bank and handle collections at BBVA. Wealth management added eight use cases to reach 45, and 18 banks now disclose realised or projected AI value.
top.why: Deployment is running ahead of proof: banks seeking AI budgets for 2027 will face boards asking for outcomes that most peers still do not publish.

items.headline: Update: Zug pension fund says members' data may be in PK Softech theft
items.summary: Pensionskasse Zug said its members' data may have been taken in the cyberattack on PK Softech, software supplier to its outsourced administrator Libera. Told of the incident in mid-October, it believed it was unaffected until last week. The data held included names, AHV numbers, birth dates, addresses and salaries; the fund has informed the FDPIC.
items.why: Shows how far one vendor breach travels through outsourced chains: funds that thought they were clear can learn weeks later that they are not.

items.headline: Update: Arkéa attackers stole about EUR 100 million through a supplier's platform, Reuters says
items.summary: Attackers stole around EUR 100 million from Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, according to Reuters as reported by Fintech News Switzerland; the bank acknowledged the approximate scale without confirming the figure. They entered through a third-party service provider's platform and used the bank's own account to move funds; some were blocked, and almost all operations resumed on 4 November.
items.why: Entry through a supplier's platform is the third-party risk DORA was written for, and a concrete case for boards reviewing their own provider access.

items.headline: Survey: 82 percent of banks use generative AI in credit and risk decisions
items.summary: A survey of 300 credit, treasury and risk leaders at banks in 31 countries, by FT Longitude, SAS and Microsoft, found 82 percent use generative AI and 41 percent agentic AI in decision-making, according to Fintech News Singapore. 59 percent have moved beyond experimentation, though only 15 percent report widespread embedding.
items.why: Credit and risk are where supervisors look hardest at model governance, so adoption at this level raises the workload for validation and explainability teams.

items.headline: Dallas Fed survey: 11.4 percent of banks already restrict customers' AI agents
items.summary: In a Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas survey of 70 bankers, 11.4 percent said their institution or service provider had restricted customers' AI agents on online banking, and 22.9 percent planned to within six months, according to PYMNTS. Another 27.1 percent did not know.
items.why: Policies on customer-side agents are forming bank by bank, leaving authentication, liability and fraud rules for agent access unsettled across the industry.

items.headline: UBS expects Swiss wages to rise 1 percent in 2027, barely ahead of inflation
items.summary: UBS's new salary survey expects nominal wages in Switzerland to rise 1 percent in 2027 against inflation of 0.8 percent, real growth of 0.2 percent, according to ICTjournal. IT and telecoms pay, which UBS had expected to rise 1.7 percent in 2026, rose 1 percent and is forecast to match the national average.
items.why: Restrained pay keeps cost growth low in Swiss banks' 2027 budgets, while employers give AI skills growing weight, especially when hiring juniors.

items.headline: UniCredit earns a record EUR 3.3 billion and could control Commerzbank this year
items.summary: UniCredit reported record third-quarter net profit of EUR 3.3 billion, up 24 percent, with a 25.5 percent return on tangible equity, according to finews.ch. It expects the last approvals for a larger Commerzbank stake by the end of November, followed by an extraordinary meeting to elect new supervisory board members.
items.why: A merger of HypoVereinsbank and Commerzbank, now possibly earlier than after 2028, would bring a large German core systems and data integration forward.

items.headline: CFA Institute council ranks AI-driven cyberattacks among four most immediate systemic risks
items.summary: The CFA Institute Systemic Risk Council ranked geopolitical shocks, AI-driven cyberattacks, opaque data-centre financings and sudden extreme climate events as the most immediate of 13 threats to financial stability, according to WealthBriefing. It said each could disrupt critical infrastructure or freeze international capital markets within hours.
items.why: Puts AI-enabled attacks and the debt behind AI data centres on the same list as geopolitics, a framing that bank risk committees are likely to borrow.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Ember, a low-cost model for high-volume agent work
items.summary: Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember, its lightest and cheapest model, at 10 cents per million input tokens, built for tool calls, routing, extraction and long-document parsing, according to TechCrunch. It reads text, images and audio and is designed to work under the larger Muse Wonder: Wonder plans, Ember handles the volume.
items.why: A cheap multimodal worker under a planning model lowers the cost of automating high-volume tasks such as document extraction and case triage in back offices.

items.headline: Google adds TPU 8tx for confidential inference and TPU 8i Max for long contexts
items.summary: Google added two eighth-generation TPU systems: TPU 8tx, with hardware-level security for sensitive data, and TPU 8i Max, for very large context windows. Google says TPUs now have nearly 100 customers, including frontier labs and trading firms, and customers can also deploy them in their own data centres.
items.why: Hardware-level protection for inference answers a standard objection from banks handling client-identifying data, and on-premises TPUs widen the options for regulated workloads.

items.headline: Databricks will launch on AWS's European Sovereign Cloud and contract through an EU entity
items.summary: Databricks said it will launch on the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and is committed to making Azure Databricks meet EU sovereignty requirements. European customers can now contract directly with a Databricks EU entity; the company serves them from 17 European cloud regions.
items.why: Sovereign hosting and a local contracting entity remove two frequent procurement hurdles for European banks and insurers standardising their data platforms.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic plans to set its IPO price range this week, WSJ reports
items.summary: Anthropic plans to set a valuation range this week and begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week, The Wall Street Journal reported, according to TechCrunch. Some institutional investors are pushing for a valuation below the USD 1.5 trillion target discussed as recently as last week.
items.why: The pricing will set a public-market reference for frontier AI valuations, which boards will weigh in their own AI spending debates.
